channel.title: HKP4 · Four Lenses on Hong Kong
channel.description: Prosperity · Projection · Prospect · Potential — reading Hong Kong in depth through facts and logic

item.title: The Church Is Not Outside the Law: A Mass for the Wang Fuk Court Dead Is Proper, Insinuation Is Not
item.description: Cardinal Stephen Chow asked every parish to offer a Mass on 26 November for the dead of Wang Fuk Court. The prayer then speaks of holding to truth and practising justice. Father Joseph Ha called the letter a direction steadied in the storm. Mourning is entirely proper. Truth and justice with no owner are insinuation. A Father who raises himself on the grief of orphans is a charlatan, not a pastor. The church is protected by law, and it stands inside the law.

item.title: The Lai and Wong Cases: Which Step of Asking a Foreign Power to Sanction Your Own Country Was Democratic? The Concept-Swapping Show Has to End
item.description: Jimmy Lai drew 20 years, Joshua Wong 10, and within a week of sentencing more than a dozen voices, from international groups and Western politicians to exiled op-edists, recast the security-law cases as a blow to democracy. We lay their own words next to the judgments and the West's own precedents: those who swap the concept recast a trial of conduct as a trial of opinion. Democracy argues inside the house; collusion works outside it.

item.title: Wang Fuk Court at One Year: The Missing Pieces of the Puzzle, Completed in Court
item.description: An Orient Daily front-page interview: five residents and bereaved relatives say the apology rang hollow, the report is a jigsaw with pieces missing, and accountability has not yet reached the bottom. We answer point by point: where the pieces are held and who will set them; and an apology's sincerity is found not in wording but in what is done next.

item.title: Wang Fuk Court: A Fire Drill on the Anniversary Day — a Calendar Slip, and a Failure of Heart
item.description: The Housing Society scheduled a fire drill at the estate housing most Wang Fuk Court survivors on 26 November, the fire's anniversary, at the fire's own hour. It apologised and postponed within a day. A date can be rescheduled; thoughtlessness is the harder repair.

item.title: Wang Fuk Court: True Responsibility May Lie in Thinking About How to Move Forward
item.description: 337 days after the Tai Po fire: apology, accountability, 120 reforms and new homes, all delivered. On the eve of the anniversary we set the three claims of the critics, minimum charge, 41 blacked-out pages and the script, back before the facts to see which survive. Honouring the dead is done by moving forward.

item.title: The Joshua Wong Sentence: The Legal Basis, the Factual Basis, and a Political Show That Opened Exactly on Cue
item.description: Ten years rests on law and on evidence. The density of the international reactions — ten foreign governments and a roster of NGOs, all in step within 24 hours — proves the stage was waiting, not that justice was shocked.

item.title: One Country Is the Foundation, Hong Kong's System Is the Space — HKP4 Founding Editorial
item.description: One country, two systems: the one country is the foundation of everything; Hong Kong's system is the space for development. This is where all of our observation begins.
